summary: The coordinate-slice inheritance and binary-coordinate equality are valid for the canonical integral hitting families and original weights. Affine injection preserves barycentric supports and logarithmic gaps, and coordinate extrema force ambient supports into their slice when the sliced factors have at most two positive entries. With at most one active retained coefficient, every nonempty slice is a product of nonzero finite globally extendable log-concave factors, including the correctly truncated factor. The accepted product theorem in positive dimension r and the mass partition over N slices give the claimed bound. Empty T, singleton supports, inactive budgets, either sign of the retained coefficient, and budget-boundary points introduce no errors or gaps.
